A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RFC-based audit of hallucinations in reasoning models. The text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–F support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset statistics, behavioral annotations, CoT intervention experiments, and hallucination-detector evaluations, including additional analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds cross-model evaluations, hallucination-frequency analysis, and a neutral-prompt factuality experiment in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The CoT graph framework, dataset construction Algorithms 1–3, prompt templates, and edit-and-continue interventions are retained. Expanded descriptions of reflection, metacognition, and annotation do not establish a change to the underlying procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix B.8 adds binary factuality judgment under a neutral prompt, using true and false statements from the Type II source pool. This introduces a distinct task and prompt condition, while the RFC domain and four original dataset subsets remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Appendix B.2 adds Claude-3.7-Sonnet and Qwen3 to the reported model comparisons alongside DeepSeek-R1. The seven hallucination-detection methods in Table 3 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include evaluating additional models on DeepSeek-filtered subsets, a two-of-three query acceptance criterion, grouping chains by hallucination frequency, and neutral judgments of 500 true plus 500 false statements. Original experimental settings are retained. New GPT-4o annotation wording conflicts with the retained GPT-4o-mini description, so an actual annotator switch is not established.

E4.justification: v2 adds substantial checks of generality across models (B.2), the association between hallucination frequency and chain length (B.7), and whether factual competence under neutral prompts supports the prompt-bias explanation (B.8). These extend the original intervention analyses and detector case studies to several previously untested questions.

E5.justification: B.2 newly reports three attempts per query for the added comparison. The original five-answer construction and Table 3 uncertainty entries are retained; B.7 analyzes the existing five-run structure rather than establishing additional runs. No new confidence intervals or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: Tables 6–9 add cross-model rates, chain-length results by hallucination frequency, and factual judgments correctly classifying 478/500 true and 487/500 false statements. Original main tables and segment-wise CCP results are unchanged. New Table 6 reports DeepSeek-R1 Type II Control acceptance as 11.0%, inconsistent with the retained 92/863 (10.66%) in Table 1.

T1.justification: New Appendix E.3 introduces an approximate inference-cost model and derives costs including 17.2ST for Semantic Entropy, 1.8ST for CCP, and 20T for Self-Check. The central hallucination assumptions and Equations (1)–(4) retain their mathematical substance.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same claims about erroneous-knowledge propagation, reflection and prompt alignment, resistance to editing, and detector limitations. Additional appendix evidence does not redefine the main contribution.

C2.justification: B.8 strengthens the interpretation that Type II failures reflect prompt-aligned bias rather than simple knowledge absence. B.2 extends the interpretation across model families while acknowledging differently filtered samples. Section 2.3 more explicitly distinguishes confidence in knowing a claim from factual correctness, and Appendix A develops plans for quantitative validation.

D1.justification: C.1 adds annotation-category criteria, a 10% manual review disclosure, and iterative label refinement. E.3 supplies typical sampling counts and cost assumptions. The code hyperlink changes from an anonymous repository to an identified GitHub repository; existing hardware specifications and prompt templates are retained.

R1.justification: Six references are added on knowledge storage, sycophancy, metacognition, and self-reflection, including Kadavath et al., Griot et al., and MIRROR. They contextualize the expanded explanations without replacing the existing related-work framework or novelty positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes focused rewrites in Sections 2.2–2.3 and 4, adds an experimental overview and appendix subsections, and updates author information and acknowledgements. The overall narrative and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Four appendix tables are added, Figures 1–2 receive expanded captions, and the retained keyword pie charts are arranged side by side. Figure 2's caption newly discloses trace truncation and shifted rejection timing. Existing diagrams and plots are retained, with other changes mainly involving placement and reflow.

improvement.justification: The added factuality control and cross-model tests broaden the empirical evidence, while annotation criteria and clearer confidence explanations improve transparency. The gain remains limited: differently filtered model samples and unmeasured confidence dynamics constrain the stronger mechanism interpretations, and v2 introduces small numerical and annotation-model inconsistencies.
